title: Zigbee 3.0 mesh: ESP32-H2, roles, and Home Assistant

spans.text: Zigbee is a low-power networking protocol for sensors and controls. It requires a chip with IEEE 802.15.4 radio, such as ESP32-H2 or ESP32-C6.

A Zigbee network has one Coordinator that forms the network and admits nodes; Routers forward traffic and are normally always powered; End Devices can be sleepy battery sensors that send through a parent but do not route messages. Routers extend mesh coverage. Zigbee 3.0 uses interoperable application profiles and ZCL clusters, such as On/Off `0x0006` and Temperature Measurement `0x0402`.

Espressif's Zigbee SDK is an ESP-IDF project, not a generic Arduino UNO library. Its official `home_automation_devices/on_off_light` example runs as a Coordinator on H2/C6 and handles On/Off cluster commands. For Home Assistant with Zigbee2MQTT, a compatible radio needs coordinator firmware and a supported serial/protocol integration; an arbitrary ESP32 Zigbee application is not automatically a ready adapter. Zigbee2MQTT exposes devices to Home Assistant through an MQTT broker.
Build the official ESP-IDF On/Off Coordinator example

spans.code:
git clone --recursive https://github.com/espressif/esp-zigbee-sdk.git
cd esp-zigbee-sdk/examples/home_automation_devices/on_off_light
idf.py set-target esp32h2
idf.py -p PORT erase_flash flash monitor

spans.title: Important safety and compatibility note
spans.text: Classic ESP32, S2, and S3 lack IEEE 802.15.4 radio; use a compatible H2/C6 board. Plan coordinator backup and secure network-key storage for production. Wi-Fi and Zigbee 2.4 GHz channels can interfere.
